title: Archons
summary: The agents who carry out the justicars' will.

claims.text: Archons serve the Camarilla in large numbers under six different masters, and no single archon has met all the others.
Each justicar keeps a separate agenda, allies and team, so archon coteries sometimes work against each other without knowing it.
Most princes and elders do not want archons in their cities, and the mere threat of one arriving can spur a slow prince to act.
Some justicars make their archons swear an oath on entering service, though the Traditions do not require it.

title: The Seventh Justicar
summary: Who might fill the seat the Gangrel left empty.

claims.text: When the Gangrel justicar left the Camarilla with most of the clan, one of the six seats fell empty and several campaigns began to fill it.
One campaign wants a justicar for the smaller bloodlines and the Caitiff, though few expect it to happen.
The likelier campaign seeks an Assamite justicar, pushed by the Gangrel loss and Sabbat moves in the East, though it is still many nights from serious debate.

title: Templars
summary: Sabbat bodyguards named after the crusading knights.

claims.text: The Sabbat took the name from the knightly order that guarded pilgrims, to give its bishops escorts, and the post soon grew beyond simple guard duty.

title: Paladins and the Table
summary: A cardinal's senior templars and council.

claims.text: Paladins are often former templars but hold a separate rank; a cardinal's Table of Twelve meets as often as needed to debate policy and advise.
Lesser Sabbat officials have lately started naming their own senior templars paladins, which a cardinal's paladin may resent.
A paladin receives a gilded, ermine-trimmed tabard; turning up to Table without it signals disapproval, and a dishonourable discharge strips it off in public.
